news.title: GNUTS Announces 2nd Central Committee Meeting for the 34th Administration
news.content:
The Ghana National Union of Technical Students (GNUTS) has officially announced the details for its 2nd Central Committee Meeting under the 34th Administration.

The high-profile student leadership meeting is scheduled to take place from 3rd to 4th September, 2026. This gathering will bring together student leaders, institutional representatives, and executives to deliberate on key policies, address student welfare concerns, and strategize on advancing technical education in Ghana.

Event Details at a Glance:

Event: 2nd Central Committee Meeting (34th GNUTS Administration)

Date: 3rd – 4th September, 2026

Venue: Kumasi Technical University, Ashanti Region

Delegates and invited student leadership figures are entreated to prepare ahead of the summit as the union continues to uphold its core motto: #BeTheDifference. For further updates and official notices, members can visit the official GNUTS portal at www.gnuts.org or follow social media handles via @gnuts_live.
news.author: GNUTS PRO

news.title: GNUTS Launches "#ChooseTVETFirst" Campaign to Champion Skills Development
news.content:
The Ghana National Union of Technical Students (GNUTS) under the 34th Administration has officially rolled out its national advocacy initiative, the "#ChooseTVETFirst" Campaign, anchored on the powerful theme: "Skills Are The Future."

This visionary campaign is designed to shift public perception, elevate the status of Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET), and encourage young people to embrace practical skills acquisition as a primary pathway to national development and sustainable employment.

Key Highlights of the Campaign:

Core Theme: Skills Are The Future (#ChooseTVETFirst)

Objective: Promoting hands-on technical training, robotics, engineering competence, and modern vocational expertise.

Initiator: Ghana National Union of Technical Students (34th Administration)

GNUTS continues to advocate for infrastructure development, innovation, and enhanced opportunities for technical students across Ghana. For more details on the campaign and how to get involved, visit the official union platform at www.gnuts.org or connect via social media channels @gnuts_live.
news.author: GNUTS PRO

scholarships.title: Chevening Scholarship (Ghana)
scholarships.description: The Chevening Scholarship is the UK Government’s prestigious international awards scheme funded by the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO). It provides full financial support for future leaders from Ghana to pursue a one-year taught master’s degree at any eligible university in the United Kingdom. The award typically covers full university tuition fees, a monthly living allowance, return economy airfares to the UK, and additional grants to cover essential academic expenses.
scholarships.requirements:
Be a citizen of Ghana and commit to returning for at least two years after the scholarship ends

Hold an undergraduate degree that qualifies you for entry to a UK master's program

Have a minimum of 2,800 hours (roughly two years) of work experience acquired after your undergraduate degree

Apply to three different, eligible one-year taught master's courses at UK universities

Valid passport or national identity document

Undergraduate degree certificate and transcripts

Two professional or academic references

Four application essays covering leadership, networking, study choice, and career plan

opportunities.title: AmaliTech Immersive Software Engineering Internship
opportunities.description:
The AmaliTech Immersive Internship Programme is a structured, paid technical internship designed to bridge the gap between classroom theory and professional software engineering environments.

Key Focus Areas: Frontend and Backend Engineering specializations where participants write code, build responsive web apps, and learn modern software workflows.

Required Skills & Eligibility:

Be a third-year bachelor's student or second-year Higher National Diploma (HND) student

Studying Computer Science, Engineering, Information Technology, or related technical programs

Good foundation in programming fundamentals and an eagerness to learn professional development pipelines

opportunities.title: Stain Studios Graphic Designer Internship
opportunities.description:
Stain Studios is a creative design agency offering a hands-on graphic design internship tailored for emerging visual communicators and students. The role involves supporting the design team with visual assets for branding, layout design, and digital projects.

Key Responsibilities: Assisting with graphics for web and social media, contributing to logo and brand identity design, image retouching, preparing files for print and digital delivery, and maintaining organized design files.

Required Skills & Eligibility:

Proficiency in industry-standard design tools (such as Adobe Photoshop, Illustrator, Figma, or similar)

Strong visual communication skills and meticulous attention to detail

Current enrollment in or recent completion of a design-related program (or equivalent practical experience)

A portfolio showcasing relevant academic, personal, or professional design work

resources.title: Constitution of the Ghana National Union of Technical Students (GNUTS)
resources.description: The official supreme legal framework governing the structure, membership, governance, rights, duties, and operational procedures of the Ghana National Union of Technical Students (GNUTS). It outlines the powers of key organs including Congress, the Central Committee, the National Executive Committee, the Judicial Council, and member institution SRCs, alongside election guidelines, financial administration rules, and schedules for institutional membership and rotation.

about_page.hero_subtitle: Empowering Technical & TVET Students Across Ghana
about_page.who_we_are_subtitle: The Recognized National Voice of Technical & TVET Students
about_page.who_we_are_content:
The Ghana National Union of Technical Students (GNUTS) is the sole democratic, non-partisan representative council for all technical and vocational education students across Ghana.

From advocating for industrial training allowances and modern laboratory equipment to participating in national education policy reform, GNUTS empowers technical students to become skilled engineers, tech pioneers, and industrial leaders.
about_page.mission_content:
To represent, unite, and empower technical students across Ghana by advocating for quality and inclusive technical education, promoting student welfare and leadership development, engaging stakeholders for national progress, and strengthening communication and participation within the union.

GNUTS is committed to ensuring that the concerns, aspirations, and contributions of technical students are reflected in national educational policies and development frameworks.
about_page.vision_content: To build a strong, credible, united, and nationally respected student union that effectively represents the collective interests of students in Technical Universities and Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) institutions across Ghana; a union that champions excellence, innovation, professionalism, accountability, and integrity in technical education, actively influences national educational policies, promotes skills development and employability, and positions technical students as indispensable contributors to Ghana’s industrial growth, socio-economic transformation, and sustainable national development.

history_milestones.title: Establishment of GNUPS
history_milestones.description: The Ghana National Union of Polytechnic Students (GNUPS) was established after technical students broke away from the National Union of Ghana Students (NUGS). This decision was driven by concerns of marginalization and the need for a dedicated national body to represent the unique academic, professional, and welfare interests of polytechnic students across Ghana.

history_milestones.title: The Tamale Declaration
history_milestones.description: GNUPS was formally operationalized at a national congress held in Tamale, where its first constitution was adopted. This historic congress, widely referred to as the Tamale Declaration, provided a legal and administrative framework for the Union and strengthened its legitimacy as the recognized voice of polytechnic students nationwide.

history_milestones.title: Transition from GNUPS to GNUTS
history_milestones.description: Following the Government of Ghana’s conversion of polytechnics into technical universities, GNUPS was rebranded as the Ghana National Union of Technical Students (GNUTS). The change reflected the evolving identity of technical students and was ratified at the First Central Committee and Mini Congress held at Tamale Technical University from December 1–4, 2016.

history_milestones.title: Public Recognition and Rebranding
history_milestones.description: GNUTS issued official press statements to announce and affirm its new identity. The Union emphasized legal compliance, institutional continuity, and urged stakeholders, media organizations, and the general public to recognize GNUTS as the legitimate national representative body of technical university students.
